record.original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G avoids every wheel W_t of order t >= 2k + 1, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.46. Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be sufficiently large. If G in G(m, {Wt : t >= 2k + 1}), then lambda(G) <= (k-1+sqrt(4m-k^2+1))/2. Equality holds if and only if G ~= Kk \/ (m/k - (k-1)/2)K1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, and let $\lambda(G)$ denote the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix (the largest eigenvalue). For an integer $t\ge 4$, the wheel $W_t$ of order $t$ is the graph obtained by joining a single vertex to every vertex of a cycle $C_{t-1}$ on $t-1$ vertices. For graphs $H_1,H_2$, write $H_1\vee H_2$ for their join (the disjoint union together with all edges between $V(H_1)$ and $V(H_2)$), and let $sK_1$ denote the empty graph on $s$ vertices.

Fix an integer $k\ge 2$ and assume $m$ is sufficiently large with $k\mid m$ (so that $m/k-(k-1)/2$ is a half-integer interpreted appropriately, or more precisely $m$ is chosen so that the extremal graph $K_k\vee (m/k-(k-1)/2)K_1$ has exactly $m$ edges). Prove or disprove: if $G$ is a graph with $m$ edges that contains no wheel $W_t$ as a subgraph for any $t\ge 2k+1$, then
$$\lambda(G)\le \frac{k-1+\sqrt{4m-k^2+1}}{2},$$
with equality if and only if $G\cong K_k\vee \bigl(\tfrac{m}{k}-\tfrac{k-1}{2}\bigr)K_1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as a conjecture for general fixed k ≥ 2. Related results exist: the maximum spectral radius of wheel-free graphs (forbidding all wheels) and Nikiforov-type spectral Turán problems by edge count have been studied, but a verification of this specific conjecture forbidding all wheels of order ≥ 2k+1 with extremal graph K_k ∨ (independent set) for all fixed k has not been located.

status_evidence.title: The maximum spectral radius of wheel-free graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Determines the maximum spectral radius of wheel-free graphs of order n and characterizes the extremal graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Related (order-based) wheel-free spectral extremal problems have been resolved, but the edge-based conjecture for general k remains stated as a conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Spectral Graph Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of unsolved spectral graph theory problems including Brualdi–Solheid–Turán type questions.
status_evidence.claim: Spectral Turán-type conjectures of this Brualdi–Solheid form are commonly open for fixed k.
